slides.title: Polygons, Polyhedra, and Patterns
slides.html:
Polygons, Polyhedra, and Patterns

I can classify polygons and see patterns in repeated shapes.

geo.title: Polygons, Polyhedra, and Patterns
geo.target: I can classify polygons and see patterns in repeated shapes.

slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Stage 0 is one shaded triangle. To make the next stage, join the midpoints of each shaded triangle's sides and remove the middle one. Hand-draw stages 0 to 3, count the shaded triangles, and predict stage 4.

  • I can classify polygons and see patterns in repeated shapes.
  • I can tell a polygon from a figure that is not a polygon, and name polygons by sides.
  • I can count parts of a pattern stage by stage and describe the rule.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: In this course, a polygon is a simple closed path of at least three nonzero straight sides. Consecutive sides meet at their common endpoint and are not collinear; nonconsecutive sides do not meet. Its polygonal region includes its boundary and interior. That region is convex if, for every two points of the region, the entire segment joining them lies in the region. (In plain words: In this course, a polygon is a closed loop of at least three straight sides, each with positive length. Only neighboring sides meet, at their shared endpoint, and neighboring sides are not on the same line. The region is the loop together with its inside. It is convex when, for any two points in that region, boundary included, the whole straight segment between them stays in the region.) A polygon is regular if all sides are equal and all angles are equal.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.html:
• polygon A closed flat path of at least three straight sides. Each side meets exactly two others, one at each end, and sides that are not neighbors never touch.
  • vertex A corner of a polygon, where two sides meet.
  • side One of the segments that make up a polygon.
  • diagonal A segment joining two corners of a polygon that are not next to each other.
  • convex For any two points in the region, inside or on the edge, the whole segment between them stays in the region.
  • regular All sides equal and all angles equal.
  • polyhedron A solid whose faces are all polygons.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Lina says, "Every dot marked on a polygon's boundary is a vertex."

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

A dot strictly inside an existing straight side is not a new vertex. A vertex is where consecutive sides meet; in our course those consecutive sides must not lie on the same line. Adding a dot or a name does not create a corner or change the polygon.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
A convex polygon has 5 sides. How many vertices and sides does it have? How many diagonals start at one chosen vertex?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

5 vertices and 5 sides. From A1 there are 4 other vertices. Two of them are next to A1, so 4 - 2 = 2 diagonals.

Reveal second check

Total diagonals: 5(5 - 3)/2 = 5. Each diagonal is counted from both ends, so divide by 2.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Someone says 'any closed curve is a polygon.' Give two shapes that break this, then fix the definition.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

A circle has no straight sides. A bow-tie has sides that cross. Fix: a polygon is a closed path of at least 3 straight sides, each longer than zero, that touch only where neighbor sides share an endpoint, with no two neighbor sides on one line.

Reveal second check

The circle fails 'straight sides.' The bow-tie fails 'no crossings.' A triangle passes both.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
Can a 4-sided shape have all sides equal but still not be regular? Give all the facts for an example.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Yes. Take a rhombus with all four sides 5 and angles 60, 120, 60 and 120 degrees. Its sides are equal, but its angles are not, so it is not regular. The angles are given; we did not work them out.

Reveal second check

Regular needs equal sides and equal angles. 60 and 120 are different, so it fails.
